newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela seen producing 3.7 mln bpd in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela seen producing 3.7 mln bpd in 1997.

text.p: Venezuelan production of crude, natural gas and derivatives will rise 500,000 barrels per day (bpd) in 1997 to reach 3.71 million bpd, according to copies of state-owned oil company PdVSA plans obtained by Reuters.

Of this amount 3.03 million bpd of crude and products will be exported, according to the plans which are due to be offically approved Friday in a closed-door meeting between PdVSA and Ministry of Energy and Mines officials.
Venezuela, which is frequently accused of busting its OPEC production quota of 2.359 million bpd, exported 2.727 million bpd of crudes and products in 1996, according to the figures.
PdVSA executives are also expected to agree a 3.12 trillion bolivar 1997 budget at the meeting.

That is equivalent to $6.37 billion at the government estimated average 1997 exchange rate of 490 bolivars per dollar - - although PdVSA has suggested using an averaged exchange rate of between 520 and 522 bolivars per dollar.
Fueled by high international oil prices and aggressive expansion plans, the budget easily tops PdVSA's 1996 spending of 1.7 trillion bolivars ($4.05 billion).

The rise comes despite a recent International Monetary Fund (IMF) recommendation that PdVSA cut nearly $1 billion from its investment plans for the coming year in order to curb inflation in the wider economy.
